transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-16 15:30 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maria (Redwood SE), Avery (Redwood SE), Dr. Anika Roy (CTO), Samir Patel (Head Infra), Leah Morris (Compliance), Diego Torres (Firmware)

--- Summary (auto-gen):
Redwood team walked through high-level architecture options for HelixPath's closed network requirement. Key unknowns: exact GPU models, firmware signing toolchain, approval cadence for patches, and whether HSM will be accessible from the update controller. Agreed to share security docs and hardware inventory; plan PoC in Jan.

00:00:03 Jordan: thanks everyone for jumping on, uh quick intros and we'll kick off, Jordan from Redwood, Maria and Avery on the technical side.
00:00:12 Anika: Hi, I'm Anika Roy, CTO at HelixPath, and I'll let Samir do the infra overview.
00:00:18 Samir: yeah hi Samir here, we run the compute clusters for inference in our datacenter, fully isolated, no outbound internet, we only have a jump box that we bring in on-site when needed.
00:00:32 Maria: okay got it, so air-gapped, jump-box based updates, can you confirm the jump box has controlled egress and is physically in the same facility?
00:00:40 Samir: correct, jump box lives in our NOC, only specific engineers have key access, and Diego manages firmware signing.
00:00:48 Diego: yeah we do a signed firmware pipeline, it's an internal tool, we need to understand how Redwood's update artifacts can be signed and verified against our chain.
00:01:02 Avery: one thing to flag, Redwood Private supports an offline bundle model where we produce an artifact that can be signed by customer KMS/HSM and then applied by your ops. The question is the format and the attestation headers.
00:01:18 Leah: from compliance we need 12 month audit retention for update logs, and redaction for patient identifiers. Also we prefer immutable audit logs stored in a remote WORM storage - but must be reachable only from within the closed network.
00:01:34 Jordan: totally reasonable. Maria, can you explain how fallback or staged rollouts work if a node fails?
00:01:40 Maria: yes, in a connected deployment we'd do canary+auto-rollback; for air-gapped, we rely on staged bundles and manual promotion. We can provide a checklist and a simulated rollback artifact so you can rehearse. Note small bit flub: our "KV cache" doc in the meeting notes sometimes comes out as "KV cash" in transcripts, but it's KV cache - it matters for warm-start performance.
00:02:07 Anika: latency is critical for our pipeline, we need sub-200ms 95th on common queries for the 6B model. We also want predictable cost per inference - trying to compare Redwood Dedicated vs Private.
00:02:20 Jordan: understood. For Private we usually recommend fixed capacity pools — predictability — but you'll be responsible for HW procurement and upgrades. We can provide batch configs and quantization profiles to meet the latency target.
00:02:34 Samir: about hardware, we currently have a mix, mostly A800s and some older A40s; BIOS versions vary, and some nodes can't update firmware remotely without a physical console.
00:02:48 Diego: and we have a strict change window: first Tuesday of month 0200-0600 local only; emergency patches by exception with CAB approval.
00:02:58 Leah: CAB is: CISO, Head of Ops, Compliance, and a clinical rep must sign off for any patch that touches models used in production.
00:03:10 Maria: that influences how we plan the PoC — if patching requires human sign-off, automated hotpatching is off the table; we can do a manual bundle release process.
00:03:22 Jordan: can you walk through the signing key flow — is the HSM reachable from your jumpbox or is it air-gapped as well?
00:03:30 Diego: the HSM is in a separate vault, you have to be on the console to sign. We have export controls, and keys are hardware-backed.
00:03:39 Avery: so Redwood will need to hand off an unsigned artifact; your team will sign, then you'll apply it locally. We support that offline signing workflow but need to verify file-level checksums and optional attestation headers.
00:03:56 Samir: what's the artifact size typically for model updates? If we need to bring them in via USB, size matters.
00:04:02 Maria: depends on model size and quantization — a 7B fully-fp16 can be tens of GB, but with quantization & sharding you can get artifacts down. For large models, incremental KV/cache warm-starts are possible so you don't always need complete re-deploy.
00:04:20 Anika: can Redwood support running smaller distilled models locally and handle heavier requests with Redwood Hosted fallback? We know there are regulatory limits, but maybe only for non-PHI queries?
00:04:33 Jordan: we can architect a hybrid: local for sensitive PHI-bound inference, hosted/dedicated fallback for lower-sensitivity batch processing. But that requires routing rules and a strict policy. Also note data residency; you'll need legal sign-off.
00:04:48 Leah: right, we can't send PHI offsite. So fallback must be opt-in per-route and scrubbed.
00:04:55 Maria: technical deep-dive: how do you handle KV cache when models run on different nodes, is the cache baked into the artifact or built at runtime?
00:05:05 Avery: cache is runtime-managed; we support prefix cache export/import to warm up nodes — we can produce a cache snapshot file you can transfer. Caveat: snapshots can contain tokens that may be considered PHI if prompts include patient text; so they'd need redaction before export.
00:05:26 Anika: ok that matters. Also curious about monitoring: we need per-token cost, latency traces, and model versioning in the console — but it must be accessible inside the closed net.
00:05:38 Jordan: Redwood Console can run as a private console inside your VPC; for fully air-gapped we offer an offline slice that you can host behind your firewall. We ship a UI bundle + metrics pipeline; metrics can be pushed to your Prometheus but the console itself can be local.
00:05:56 Samir: storage for logs — we need 7 years for certain audit trails; is the log retention configurable?
00:06:04 Jordan: yes retention is configurable; for offline deployments you control the storage lifecycle. We recommend WORM-backed object storage for immutability.
00:06:13 Leah: about legal and procurement: what SLAs can you offer for Private? We will need 99.9 uptime commitments and a runbook for escalation.
00:06:23 Jordan: SLAs on private are contractual; standard offering includes support tiers. We'll pull legal templates but that will be in the enterprise negotiation. For PoC we usually operate without SLA but with engineer support.
00:06:36 Maria: performance question — can you run quantized int8 on A800s for the 6B and still hold 200ms 95th? We have to test.
00:06:45 Avery: likely yes with tuned kernels and batching. We'll propose a benchmark matrix: model size, seq length, batch size, quant config vs measured latency.
00:06:55 Diego: firmware: we need signed boot chain for the inference nodes, and we want a hash of the model binary before deployment — can Redwood provide model hash generation?
00:07:06 Jordan: yes we can produce SHA256 of the artifact and include a manifest. We'll include provenance data: model version, config, quantization flags.
00:07:15 Anika: how about emergency rollback — if a bundle breaks inference, what's the plan?
00:07:21 Maria: staged rollout + manual revert. For air-gapped: we keep previous bundle on standby and a revert checklist. We can also provide a diagnostic artifact to collect logs for debugging without sending them offsite.
00:07:34 Samir: backup process needs to be in that runbook. Also procurement question: if we stick with Private, does Redwood help with HW sizing and procurement guidance?
00:07:44 Jordan: yes we do sizing recommendations and can provide preferred vendor lists and BOMs; we don't procure hardware for you by default but can assist via partners.
00:07:53 Leah: compliance asks: do you support signed audit logs with tamper-evident timestamps?
00:07:58 Avery: we support immutability via WORM and can append cryptographic checksums; integration with your SIEM is also possible.
00:08:08 Diego: note on physical constraints — some racks don't have NVLink support, so multi-GPU models might not be feasible. How do you handle model parallelism with limited interconnect?
00:08:19 Maria: we can recommend model sharding strategies and lower model sizes to fit a single GPU, or use pipeline parallelism with explicit network sharding but that adds latency. We'll include tradeoffs in the PoC doc.
00:08:35 Anika: timeline — we're hoping for an initial PoC in Q1, security review in Jan, procurement in Feb, and full rollout by Q2 if all goes well.
00:08:44 Jordan: sounds aligned. Next, specific asks — Samir can you share an inventory export and Leah can confirm redaction rules?
00:08:52 Samir: yes I'll export and share by 12/20.
00:08:55 Leah: I'll compile redaction rules and legal notes by 12/21.
00:08:59 Jordan: perfect. Maria will draft a PoC plan and proposed benchmark matrix.
00:09:05 Maria: i'll circulate by 12/23 and include test payloads.
00:09:10 Anika: any concerns about vendor lock-in? We need to be able to move models or run fallback in Dedicated or Hosted if needed.
00:09:18 Jordan: Redwood supports model export and you can pin to open weights; portability is a design goal. We'll document rollback and export procedures.
00:09:27 Samir: one more on encryption - do you need keys in memory unencrypted for inference? We want to minimize key exposure.
00:09:33 Avery: keys used for disk encryption or model encryption are decrypted at runtime; we recommend using HSM-backed transient keys and minimal exposure windows.
00:09:44 Diego: final note: firmware updates require signed image + audit. We'll want to test a complete cycle in staging before prod.
00:09:52 Jordan: agreed, we'll schedule an onsite hardware review with Diego and Maria week of 12/28.
00:10:00 Anika: ok thanks all, that covers most items. Quick recap?
00:10:05 Jordan: recap: Redwood to send security pack, PoC plan, and artifact signing guidance. HelixPath to share inventory and redaction rules. Set PoC to start early Jan. We'll follow up with a Doodle for the onsite.
00:10:21 Leah: thanks, meeting end.
